name: Hadadezer
bio:
Hadadezer son of Rehob was the king of Zobah, a powerful Aramean kingdom, whom David struck down while Hadadezer was on his way to restore his control along the Euphrates. David captured a thousand of his chariots, seven hundred horsemen, and twenty thousand foot soldiers, hamstringing the chariot horses except for a hundred he kept back, and went on to defeat the Arameans of Damascus who came to Hadadezer's aid (2 Samuel 8:3-6). David took the gold shields carried by Hadadezer's officers and dedicated them, along with bronze plundered from his cities — bronze later used by Solomon to make the great bronze basin, the pillars, and other bronze vessels of the temple (1 Chronicles 18:7-8) — to the LORD (2 Samuel 8:7-8, 11-12); word of Hadadezer's defeat also prompted King Toi of Hamath, his old rival, to send his own son Joram to David with gifts and congratulations (2 Samuel 8:9-10).

After the Ammonites, who had hired Aramean mercenaries against Israel, were routed by Joab and Abishai, Hadadezer summoned Arameans from beyond the Euphrates under his commander Shobach for a second attempt. David himself led Israel out to meet them at Helam and won a crushing victory, killing Shobach and the men of seven hundred chariots; the defeat was so total that every king who had served Hadadezer made peace with Israel, and the Arameans never again dared help the Ammonites (2 Samuel 10:15-19).
